mission.title: Redundancy
mission.description: Confront Ouroboros about the crisis caused by its failed parts.

npc.say:
Who? Can't say; got my own meetings to watch out for, you know? Ha-ha.
Ri-ight.
No... Uh... Try down that way.
Yeah... To tell the truth, I try not to pick up names around here. It isn't like I want to socialize with these people or anything.

... I'm afraid we're out of coffee. There should be...a drinking fountain around somewhere.
Excuse me.

Wha--
Wow, look at the time.

Hey, come back!
I know your beeper numbers!
Hey, what's that... I think I feel a touch of flu coming on--highly contagious forty-eight hour flu.
Good thing my pager stopped working this morning. There's going to be hell to pay when everything's back on line, but that's what saved vacation is for...

phase.briefing:
Operative, we have been able to quell some of the rioting in the city, but civilian casualties will continue to rise as long as the widespread shortage of functional television and Internet devices persists. The Ouroboros Corporation, as the supplier of the malfunctioning parts, should have began to furnish working replacements, but this has not occurred, and their apparent recalcitrance is only increasing customer dissatisfaction. Ouroboros must be confronted about the crisis caused by their failed parts, and provide a solution--or at least an explanation.
Agent Pace will provide you with several support units for this task.

enter.say: I'm not all that thrilled at the prospect of more Ouroboros products going into circulation anyway. How do we know they wouldn't have another mass "malfunction"?

talk.say: Saluti, {player}. These Agents will assist you in your call on the Ouroboros Corporation.

done.say: Yes; once the three of you leave, I will be left alone. Of course, as an Agent of the System, I can never be said to be truly alone--no, never.

objective.text: Lead Agent Clark and Agent Long out of the area

near.say: Why do you think you are required to speak to Agent Pace before being allowed to proceed? Is what she tells you of any direct value to the mission itself? If not, then what is the purpose of this procedure?

phase.briefing: Proceed to the Ouroboros office, operative. They have been told to expect contact from us.

enter.say: The Ouroboros honcho you'll be meeting with is some guy named Barney Rodick.

objective.text: Visit Ouroboros with Agent Clark and Agent Long

done.say: He isn't there? Uh... Better look around for him.

talk.say: Sorry, buddy; haven't got a clue. Try asking someone else?

done.say: Huh... Well, if he does show, the Agents will report it. I think something's up, though. We'd better give Gray the news.

phase.briefing: Ouroboros has flaunted a disdain for our representatives in the past, but they had not neglected to arrive at a meeting. The disorganized responses you obtained from the staff on site suggest that some unknown factor is at play. We may have more success in discovering the cause of this apparent disarray by paying an unscheduled visit to another Ouroboros office--one that works closely with Barney Rodick and his staff.

enter.say: Looks like a whole lot of Monday in there. Ready to do some nosing around?

talk.say: What do you think I can do about it? Email's down! We can't even contact IS to tell them!

done.say:
Huh, so they've got internal service outages, too.
I'd make some kind of profound statement about the fragility of prewar society due to an over-reliance on technology, but hell, it was better than having to go around sniffing each other.

near.say: So, if we all just pull together--
Oh, hell! That's manager-speak for forced overtime! I'm out of here!
What in hell is going on in there?

phase.briefing:
Hm. Ouroboros' product problems may be a symptom of an internal malaise.
The location you see marked is an Ouroboros systems support facility. Staff there should be capable of diagnosing the problems.

enter.say: Corporate internal support departments are usually sucking down more bandwidth than the rest of the company put together, but I'm hardly picking up any data movement there.

done.say:
Geez, how clueless can people get?
Hm... I'm picking up some data corruption on that machine: just the kind of errors that start to crop up without proper maintenance. It's also having trouble connecting to some shared network resources... Oy, the error log looks like two Sentinels in a wrestling match.
Uh-oh, I think you've drawn attention of the shiny-helmet variety. Well, I don't see any actual useful data there, anyway.

near.say: I just don't know what it could be, then.
I wonder if we have a backup...
Well, I'm all out of ideas.

mission.finish:
The sudden failures cascading through Ouroboros services must have an intelligent origin. This cause must be found before more failures occur.
Hm... And I believe we will have to arrange for a more...reliable company to fulfill Ouroboros' failed public service contracts.
